Indicator Name: Digital health prioritized at the national level through dedicated bodies / mechanisms for governance
Assessment / Evidence: Governance structure is formally constituted though not fully-functional or meeting regularly.

Indicator Name: Digital Health prioritized at the national level through planning
Assessment / Evidence: Digital health is included in national health or relevant national strategies and/or plans.

Indicator Name: Health is prioritized in national digital transformation and data governance policies
Assessment / Evidence: National digital transformation and data governance policies do not include potential benefits and risks on public health or individual health outcomes.

Indicator Name: Readiness for emerging technologies adoption and governance
Assessment / Evidence: A plan was developed for at least one emerging technology (e.g., AI, Wearables, Blockchain, IoT) to support public health goals, but it is not being implemented.

Indicator Name: Diversity, Equity, and human rights analysis, planning and monitoring included in national digital health strategies and plans
Assessment / Evidence: Digital health strategies and programs are developed and implemented without consideration of equity and human rights implications.

Indicator Name: Gender considerations accounted for in digital health strategies and digital health governance
Assessment / Evidence: Digital health strategies and interventions are developed and implemented without consideration of gender norms, roles, and relations.

Indicator Name: National eHealth/ Digital Health Strategy or Framework
Assessment / Evidence: National digital health strategy or framework approved.

Indicator Name: National digital strategy alignment with Universal Health Coverage (UHC) Core Components
Assessment / Evidence: Digital health strategy exists and is partly aligned to UHC, addressing only one core UHC component of coverage, access, uptake, quality, and equity.

Indicator Name: Public funding for digital health
Assessment / Evidence: Non-systematic budget allocated for digital health exists or are projects and/or system-based.

Indicator Name: Private sector participation and investments in digital health
Assessment / Evidence: The private sector participation and investment in the country's digital health activities and investment is ad-hoc and limited.

Indicator Name: Legal Framework for Data Protection (Security/ Cybersecurity)
Assessment / Evidence: There is a law on data security relevant to digital health that has been proposed and is under review.

Indicator Name: Laws or Regulations for privacy, consent, confidentiality and access to health information (Privacy)
Assessment / Evidence: There is a law to protect individual privacy, governing ownership, consent, access and sharing of individually identifiable digital health data that has been proposed and is under review.

Indicator Name: Protocol for regulating or certifying devices and/or health services- including provisions for AI and algorithms (at higher stages of maturity)
Assessment / Evidence: There are no protocols, policies, frameworks or accepted processes governing the clinical and patient care use of connected medical devices and health services, particularly in relation to safety, data integrity and quality of care.

Indicator Name: Protocol for regulating and certifying AI within health services
Assessment / Evidence: There are no protocols, policies, frameworks, or accepted processes governing AI use in health services.

Indicator Name: Cross-border data security and sharing
Assessment / Evidence: There are no protocols, policies, frameworks or accepted processes in place to support secure cross-border data exchange and storage while protecting individual privacy.

Indicator Name: Digital health integrated in health and related professional pre-service training (prior to deployment)
Assessment / Evidence: Digital health curriculum proposed and under review as part of pre-service training requirements.

Indicator Name: Digital health integrated in health and related professional in-service training (after to deployment)
Assessment / Evidence: Digital health curriculum proposed and under review as part of in-service (continuing education) training for health professionals in the workforce.

Indicator Name: Training of digital health workforce
Assessment / Evidence: Professional training is available, but graduates are not yet deployed.

Indicator Name: Maturity of public sector digital health professional careers
Assessment / Evidence: A national needs assessment shows the number and types of skills needed to support digital health with an explicit focus on training cadres of female health workers.

Indicator Name: National digital health architecture and/or health information exchange
Assessment / Evidence: There is no national digital health (eHealth) architectural framework and/or health information exchange (HIE) established.

Indicator Name: Health information standards
Assessment / Evidence: There are some digital health / health information standards for data exchange, transmission, messaging, security, privacy, and hardware that have been adopted and/or are used.

Indicator Name: Network readiness
Planning and support for ongoing digital health infrastructure maintenance
Assessment / Evidence: A plan for supporting digital health infrastructure provision and maintenance has been implemented partially, but not consistently, with an estimated 0-25% of necessary infrastructure in public healthcare available and in use.

Indicator Name: Nationally scaled digital health systems
Assessment / Evidence: Some national priority areas supported by scaled digital health systems (25-50% of priority areas).

Indicator Name: Digital identity management of service providers, administrators, and facilities for digital health, including location data for GIS mapping
Assessment / Evidence: Health system registries of uniquely identifiable providers, administrators, and public facilities (and private if applicable) are being developed but are not available for use.

Indicator Name: Digital identity management of individuals for health
Assessment / Evidence: A secure registry exists, but is incomplete / partially available, used, and irregularly maintained.

Indicator Name: Digital identity management of individuals for health — Master Patient Index
Assessment / Evidence: A master patient index exists, but is incomplete / partially available, used, and irregularly maintained.

Indicator Name: Digital identity management of individuals for health — Birth Registry
Assessment / Evidence: A secure birth registry exists, is available and in active use and includes <25% of the relevant population.

Indicator Name: Digital identity management of individuals for health — Death Registry
Assessment / Evidence: A secure death registry exists, is available and in active use and includes <25% of the relevant population.

Indicator Name: Secure Patient Feedback Systems
Assessment / Evidence: No secure patient feedback system exists.

Indicator Name: Population health management contribution of digital health
Assessment / Evidence: Digital systems are used at facility or community levels and contribute to the country's public health reporting and decision-making for population health management.
